title: Multiplying Binomials
subject: Mathematics
subtopic: Products of binomials and squaring a binomial

scenes.heading: Multiplying Binomials
scenes.narration: Welcome to part one of our Grade 9 algebra series. In this lesson we multiply binomials, square a binomial, and meet the difference of two squares.

scenes.heading: What is a binomial?
bullets: A binomial has two terms, like $x + 3$ or $2a - 5$
To multiply two binomials, multiply every term in the first by every term in the second
scenes.narration: A binomial is an expression with two terms, like x plus three, or two a minus five. To multiply two binomials, multiply every term in the first bracket by every term in the second bracket. Then simplify the like terms.

scenes.heading: Example 1
scenes.narration: Multiply x plus three, by x plus five. x times x is x squared. x times five is five x. Three times x is three x. Three times five is fifteen. Add the middle terms: five x plus three x is eight x. The answer is x squared, plus eight x, plus fifteen.

scenes.heading: Example 2
scenes.narration: Multiply two x minus one, by x plus four. Two x times x is two x squared. Two x times four is eight x. Negative one times x is negative x. Negative one times four is negative four. Eight x minus x is seven x. So we get two x squared, plus seven x, minus four.

scenes.heading: Squaring a binomial
scenes.narration: x plus four, squared, means x plus four times x plus four. Multiply out: x squared, plus four x, plus four x, plus sixteen. So the answer is x squared, plus eight x, plus sixteen.

scenes.heading: A common mistake
bullets: Do not forget the middle term: $2 \times x \times 4 = 8x$
scenes.narration: A very common mistake is to write x plus four squared as x squared plus sixteen. That is wrong, because it leaves out the middle term, which is two times x times four, eight x. In general, a plus b squared is a squared, plus two a b, plus b squared. And a minus b squared is a squared, minus two a b, plus b squared.

scenes.heading: The difference of two squares
scenes.narration: Now multiply x minus six, by x plus six. We get x squared, plus six x, minus six x, minus thirty six. The middle terms cancel out, leaving x squared minus thirty six. This is called the difference of two squares.

scenes.heading: Example: Expand and simplify
scenes.narration: Expand and simplify a minus three squared, minus a plus two times a minus two. The first part is a squared, minus six a, plus nine. The second part is a squared minus four. Keep it in brackets, because the minus sign in front changes both signs. So we get a squared, minus six a, plus nine, minus a squared, plus four. The a squared terms cancel, and the answer is negative six a, plus thirteen.
